# Results — Study 908 (Optimized-Roll Commodities)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — an
**optimized-roll** commodity index (USCI: hold the 14 most-backwardated of 27 commodities,
each in its cheapest-carry contract) delivers a **higher excess-of-cash return / Sharpe**
than a **front-month** roller by dodging the "contango tax" — tested on live US ETFs
(yfinance total-return closes) with every leg taken **excess of cash (BIL)**: **USCI**
(optimized) vs **DBC** (DB "Optimum Yield", semi-optimized — the primary benchmark),
**GSG** (S&P GSCI, naive front-month) and **DJP** (Bloomberg, front-month), with **PDBC**
(optimized, 2014-11+) as a corroborating cousin. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `16935c3b46d8`.*

## Data stamp

Sample pinned as-of 2026-06-30; fingerprint `16935c3b46d8`.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **total-return** closes: USCI, DBC, PDBC, DJP, GSG, BIL — public, no key |
| Window | 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30 daily; **190** complete common months (USCI inception 2010-08-10 gates the start; PDBC from 2014-11) |
| Cash leg | **BIL** (SPDR 1-3 Month T-Bill) — every commodity leg is taken *excess of BIL*, so the shared collateral-yield (~5 %/yr in 2023-26) is netted out of both sides |
| The race | annualised **excess-of-cash Sharpe**: SR(USCI) − SR(bench); the head-to-head is the monthly return **difference** USCI − bench |
| Inference | **Newey-West HAC *t*** (6 lags) on the return difference; a **paired circular-block bootstrap** (block 6, 2000 draws, seed 908) 95 % CI on the Sharpe advantage |
| Eras | deep-contango 2010-2015 · recovery 2016-2020 · backwardation 2021-2026 |
| Costs | total returns already net each fund's **expense ratio** (USCI 1.03 %, DBC 0.85 %, GSG 0.48 %, DJP 0.70 %); an incremental bid-ask charge is added on reconstitution turnover (USCI carries the wider spread) |

> **Survivorship / short-history note (Signal axis).** All five funds are live, multi-billion
> survivors, but the *effect* is a per-month property of the wrapper, so survivorship bias is
> minor. The honest caveat is **length**: 190 months (~16 years) spanning essentially two
> commodity regimes — a thin sample for a Sharpe race, which is exactly why the sub-era cut
> below is decisive.

## Full sample — optimized wins on Sharpe, but not robustly

Excess-of-cash annualised return / vol / Sharpe, 2010-09 → 2026-06 (190 months):

| leg | excess return (%/yr) | vol (%/yr) | excess-of-cash Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **USCI (optimized)** | **+3.61** | **14.7** | **+0.245** |
| DBC (semi-optimized) | +2.34 | 17.2 | +0.136 |
| GSG (front-month) | +1.14 | 21.3 | +0.053 |
| DJP (front-month) | +0.67 | 16.5 | +0.040 |

USCI beats every benchmark — the sign the claim predicts. But the **advantage does not clear
a robust bar**:

| race | Sharpe adv | bootstrap 95 % CI | frac ≤ 0 | return diff (%/yr) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| USCI − DBC | +0.109 | [−0.130, +0.344] | 0.195 | +1.26 | +0.63 |
| USCI − GSG | +0.191 | [−0.069, +0.433] | 0.075 | +2.47 | +0.94 |
| USCI − DJP | +0.204 | [−0.027, +0.437] | 0.045 | +2.94 | +1.67 |

Every bootstrap CI **includes zero**, and no return-difference HAC *t* reaches 2. The strongest
case (vs the pure front-month DJP) is only *t* = +1.67 with a CI whose lower edge kisses zero.
Directionally consistent, statistically indistinct.

## Era cut — the edge is a contango-regime bet, not a constant premium

The full-sample win hides a **sign flip across regimes** — the single most important result:

| race | deep-contango 2010-2015 | recovery 2016-2020 | backwardation 2021-2026 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| USCI − DBC | +4.95 %/yr (*t* +1.49) | **−7.22 %/yr (*t* −3.04)** | +5.40 %/yr (*t* +1.75) |
| USCI − GSG | +7.49 %/yr (*t* +1.48) | −3.32 %/yr (*t* −0.82) | +2.86 %/yr (*t* +0.76) |
| USCI − DJP | +6.91 %/yr (*t* +2.68) | **−4.79 %/yr (*t* −2.13)** | +6.12 %/yr (*t* +2.01) |

The optimized wrapper **won big when curves were in contango (2010-2015) and again in the
2021+ backwardation/inflation surge — but *lost significantly* through the 2016-2020 recovery**,
underperforming DBC by −7.22 %/yr at *t* = −3.04 and DJP by −4.79 %/yr at *t* = −2.13. Its
backwardation/momentum screen concentrated it into the wrong commodities during that whipsaw.
An edge that is significantly *negative* in a whole five-year era is **not era-robust** — it
fails the Real bar by the desk's own rail.

## Corroborating cousin — PDBC (optimized, 2014-11+) vs front-month GSG

| race | n | Sharpe adv | bootstrap 95 % CI | return diff (%/yr) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| PDBC − GSG | 139 | +0.101 | [−0.051, +0.245] | +1.31 | +0.65 |

The second optimized wrapper tells the same story: a small positive tilt, CI through zero,
*t* well under 2. Consistent direction, no robustness.

## Costs barely move it — so costs are not the story

Total returns already embed each fund's expense ratio (so this race is *already* net of USCI's
steep 1.03 % vs GSG's 0.48 %). Adding an incremental bid-ask charge on reconstitution turnover
(USCI the wider spread) leaves the picture essentially unchanged:

| race | net Sharpe adv | net return diff (%/yr) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| USCI − DBC | +0.094 | +1.06 | +0.53 |
| USCI − GSG | +0.175 | +2.27 | +0.87 |
| USCI − DJP | +0.197 | +2.86 | +1.63 |

Because both legs are buy-and-hold, trading costs are near-irrelevant; the reason you can't bank
the edge is not friction but **regime-dependence and a hidden composition tilt** — USCI's lower
vol (14.7 % vs GSG's 21.3 %) reflects its lighter energy weight, so much of the raw Sharpe gap
is *less-concentrated-beta*, not a robustly paid roll premium.

## Total-return & drawdown context (2010-09 → 2026-06)

| fund | total return (%/yr) | max drawdown | expense ratio |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| USCI | +3.95 | −64.0 % | 1.03 % |
| DBC | +2.24 | −64.8 % | 0.85 % |
| GSG | +0.18 | −78.2 % | 0.48 % |
| DJP | +0.66 | −69.4 % | 0.70 % |

USCI did end the sample ahead with the shallowest drawdown — a genuinely nicer ride — but all
four are deeply-drawn-down commodity vehicles, and the ranking is a two-regime coin with the
optimized wrapper on the right side of it *on this particular tape*.

## Synthetic control — the machinery is faithful *(never market evidence)*

Deterministic world (`synthetic_world`, seed 908): a shared spot factor; the front index eats a
fixed contango drag; the optimized index recovers `roll_edge_annual` of it.

| planted roll edge | recovered Sharpe adv | bootstrap 95 % CI | return diff (%/yr) | HAC *t* |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 %/yr (null) | +0.007 | [−0.079, +0.100] | +0.10 | +0.14 |
| +3 %/yr | +0.194 | [+0.109, +0.292] | +3.10 | +4.27 |

The zero-edge null does not fire; a planted +3 %/yr roll edge is recovered at +3.10 %/yr, *t* =
+4.27, with a CI clear of zero. The estimator is unbiased and *would* light up a genuine,
constant roll edge at this sample size — so the real-tape failure to clear the bar is a property
of the tape (regime-flipping, thin), not of the machinery.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The optimized wrapper wins the full-sample excess-of-cash Sharpe race
  against every benchmark (USCI +0.245 vs DBC +0.14 / GSG +0.05 / DJP +0.04) — the *right sign*
  for a structural roll-yield edge, and PDBC corroborates the direction. But **no
  return-difference clears HAC *t* ≥ 2** (best +1.67 vs DJP), **every bootstrap Sharpe-advantage
  CI includes zero**, and the edge is **not era-robust**: it is significantly *negative* through
  2016-2020 (−7.22 %/yr vs DBC at *t* = −3.04; −4.79 %/yr vs DJP at *t* = −2.13) before recovering
  post-2021. A directionally-correct, economically-sensible pickup that a 16-year, two-regime
  tape cannot establish as real — **Weak, not Real.**
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Costs don't kill it (the race is already net of expense ratios; both
  legs are buy-and-hold), and USCI even ended ahead with the shallowest drawdown — but there is
  no *bankable* edge to harvest: the isolation advantage's bootstrap CI straddles zero, the sign
  flips by regime, and the raw Sharpe gap is substantially a **hidden composition tilt** (USCI's
  lower energy weight → lower vol) rather than a robustly paid roll premium. "Buy the optimized
  wrapper to pocket the roll" is, on this tape, a **contango-regime bet wearing a free-lunch
  label** — Mirage.
